subject: Order form questions — invoice recipient, tax allocation, and min commit
messages:
From: Tara Patel <tara@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoice & tax allocation

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the proposal — our procurement team reviewed the draft order form and has a few items we need clarification on before routing to legal:

- Invoice recipient: can invoices be issued to Nimbus Cloud Solutions, Inc. (EIN 12-3456789) rather than the UK parent? We need a US-billed invoice for bookkeeping.
- Tax allocation: the draft says "customer responsible for all taxes" — do you have precedent for splitting VAT/GST vs. sales/use tax? Our tax team is asking whether Redwood can handle VAT for APAC billing if applicable.
- Net terms: standard for us is Net 45; the draft lists Net 30. Any flexibility here?
- Minimum commit: can we move the minimum-commit trigger date to alignment with our FY start (Apr 1) rather than signature date?

Can we hop on a 30-min call this week? If easier, send a redline with suggested language and we can route internally.

Thanks,
Tara Patel
Sr. Procurement Manager, Nimbus Cloud Solutions
procurement@nimbuscloud.com

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Tara Patel <tara@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice & tax allocation

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear list. I chatted with finance/legal and attached a redline that addresses each point (attached: Redwood_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx). Quick summary below and proposed next steps:

- Invoice recipient: we can issue invoices to the US entity (Nimbus Cloud Solutions, Inc.) — we'll need your W-9 and billing contact.
- Tax allocation: our standard is customer pays applicable taxes. For VAT in APAC/EU, we can offer two options: (1) customer self-assesses VAT (default), or (2) Redwood invoices gross and remits VAT where Redwood has nexus — this is only for select territories and requires a separate tax annex.
- Net terms: finance can agree to Net 45 for customers who meet a minimum annual commit or prepay schedule. For this deal we can accept Net 45 if the annual committed spend is increased by 10% (or we keep Net 30 and keep original commit).
- Minimum commit effective date: we can change the trigger to the start of your fiscal quarter (Apr 1) — legal prefers an explicit clause for the "Commitment Start Date."

Next steps I propose: you confirm billing entity + provide W-9, we lock the preferred VAT handling option, and legal (Lauren) will sign off on the redlines. If that plan looks good I can set up a 30-min call with procurement + finance + legal.

Attaching redline now.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (document stub - redlined order form)

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — quick legal/finance check on Nimbus asks

Lauren / Karthik — looping you in for quick sign-off before I send everything back to Tara. Key points:

1) Net terms: finance indicated Net 45 if we increase annual committed spend by 10% (call it "Commit Threshold Adjustment"). Is that acceptable to legal from a contract enforceability perspective?
2) VAT handling: Tara wants Redwood to assume VAT for APAC if Redwood invoices gross. Do we have a standard tax annex that covers limited territory VAT remittance and indemnity language?
3) Commitment start date: they asked to make start date Apr 1. Legal commented previously that start date has to be unambiguous and tied to an explicit definition — can we accept an explicit calendar-date clause here?

I attached the redline for context. I can take any suggested language and send back to Tara the same day.

Thanks — Jonas

Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx

---
From: Tara Patel <tara@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: finance-team@nimbuscloud.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice & tax allocation

Jonas — appreciate the quick turnaround and redline. A few follow-ups from finance:

- W-9: attached W-9 (W-9-Nimbus-2027.pdf). Please confirm invoice name and remit-to address; we prefer invoices sent to AP: invoices@nimbuscloud.com.
- Net 45: procurement is okay with the Net 45 if Redwood confirms the 10% uplift threshold in writing. Please include a short note in the order form referencing the threshold calculation.
- VAT: we will self-assess VAT where we have local VAT obligations. For any APAC territories where Redwood must remit VAT, we need advance notice and a capped liability clause — can you add a cap equal to the VAT invoiced for that period?

If you can update the redline with these three items I can push to our legal. We are aiming to execute before Apr 1 so the commitment start aligns with our FY.

Thanks,
Tara
Sr. Procurement Manager
Nimbus Cloud Solutions
procurement@nimbuscloud.com
Attachment: W-9-Nimbus-2027.pdf

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Tara Patel <tara@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final — updated order form & next steps

Tara — thanks for the confirmation. We've updated the redline with the requested language and include an explicit formula for the 10% Commit Threshold Adjustment (see Section 2.1.1). Summary of changes:

- Invoice recipient: Redwood will bill Nimbus Cloud Solutions, Inc.; remit-to and AP email confirmed as invoices@nimbuscloud.com.
- W-9: received — we've recorded US tax ID for invoice issuance.
- Net terms: Net 45 accepted conditioned on the 10% uplift; language added that calculates the uplift on the Annual Committed Spend as defined in the Order Form.
- VAT: added a tax annex option that allows Redwood to invoice gross and remit VAT for specified territories, with a capped liability equal to the VAT invoiced for the period and a 30-day advance notice requirement.
- Commitment start date: explicitly set to Apr 1, 2027 in the Commitment Start Date clause.

Attached is the final order form and a DocuSign envelope link for signatures. If this aligns, please confirm and I'll send the DocuSign to your signing team.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/embeddedSigning/abc123
